turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Okay, let's start. Today we lock the self-serve pricing for Kitepost, so sales can quote it and Arjun's team can build billing against it.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Before we get into tiers, keep one number in mind. Our cost per tracked shipment is about 1.8 rupees, once you include WhatsApp messages and map lookups.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Fine. So the proposal on the table is three tiers: Starter, Growth and Enterprise, with Enterprise staying sales-led.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: And I want Starter at 3,999 rupees a month. Trackwise charges small shippers 3,999, and they are who we lose deals to.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: At 3,999 with fifteen hundred shipments included, a busy Starter account runs at about 32 percent margin. I can't sign off on that.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: Most Starter accounts won't come close to fifteen hundred. The Saffron Basket pilot averaged around nine hundred shipments a month.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Saffron Basket is one customer. I'd rather price for the busy accounts and be pleasantly surprised by the quiet ones.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Can I add the engineering angle? If we cap included shipments and charge overage, the base price matters less, because heavy users pay their own way.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: That's where I was going too. Rahul, what overage rate per shipment keeps us safe on margin?

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Four rupees per extra shipment. That's more than double our cost, and still cheaper than what Trackwise charges for overage.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: Four rupees is fine. Customers accept overage if the dashboard shows it to them before the invoice does.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Which means we need a usage meter in the product. Right now we only count shipments in the nightly billing job.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Okay, let me propose something concrete. Starter at 4,999 rupees a month, fifteen hundred shipments included, and four rupees per shipment after that.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: I still think 4,999 makes the first sales call harder. But with a visible usage meter, I can sell it.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: I'm comfortable with 4,999. That keeps a busy Starter account at around 46 percent margin.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Then that's decided. We'll go with the 4,999 rupee Starter tier, with fifteen hundred shipments and four rupee overage.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Noted on Starter. And for the Growth tier, are we still holding at 14,999 a month?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yes, 14,999 for ten thousand shipments, plus WhatsApp delivery updates and two warehouse locations.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: Monsoon Apparel asked about Growth last week. They run three warehouses, so two locations won't cover them.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Then Monsoon is an Enterprise conversation. Let's not bend the Growth tier around a single account.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: Fair enough. I'll take Monsoon Apparel through the Enterprise proposal next week instead.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Next, annual billing. Meera, you wanted twenty percent off for annual plans, right?

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: Twenty percent. Annual prepay is how we get cash up front from small businesses, and twenty is what makes people actually choose it.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Twenty is too much. At twenty percent off, the Starter margin gets thin again. I'd cap the annual discount at fifteen.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: Fifteen percent doesn't move anyone. Nobody switches to annual billing for fifteen percent.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Our own data says otherwise. Forty percent of the Saffron Basket cohort picked annual billing at only twelve percent off.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Is that cohort big enough to trust, though? If I remember right, it was only about thirty accounts.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: It was 34 accounts. Small, I agree, but it's the only real annual billing data we have so far.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I'm going to side with Rahul on this one. The annual discount is fifteen percent, and we revisit it after ninety days of real data.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: Okay. I'm not thrilled, but fifteen percent with a review at ninety days is something I can live with.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: On the build side, the usage meter is the real blocker. Billing can't go live without it, and sales can't demo overage.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Arjun, can you ship the usage meter by Friday? Almost everything else on the launch plan depends on it.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Friday works. I'll have it on staging Thursday night, with a warning banner at ninety percent of the plan limit.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: For sales, I need a revised deck with the new tiers. Saffron Basket's renewal call is on Friday, so I'll send them the revised deck by Thursday.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: And I'll set up the billing plans in Razorpay by Wednesday: monthly and annual for both Starter and Growth. Enterprise stays on manual invoices.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Thanks, Rahul. Now the launch date. I want self-serve live on Monday, November second.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: November second is tight but doable, if the pricing page is final by next week. We need the copy to build the signup flow.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: That one's on me. I'll draft the pricing page and the FAQ by Monday, including worked overage examples.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: Put a real example in the FAQ. Two thousand shipments on Starter comes to 6,999 rupees in total, and people should see that math.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Good, that example goes in. So we're agreed: self-serve launches on Monday, November second.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: One risk on that date. GST invoicing through Razorpay needs our new tax registration, and that isn't confirmed yet.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Rahul, can you chase the tax registration and confirm it either way by next Tuesday?

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Yes, I'll confirm the GST registration by next Tuesday. If it slips, we launch with manual invoices for the first week.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Let me recap the decisions. Starter is 4,999 with fifteen hundred shipments, the annual discount is fifteen percent, and we launch on November second.

turns.speaker: Meera
turns.text: And the owners: Arjun has the usage meter by Friday, I have the Saffron Basket deck by Thursday, Rahul has Razorpay by Wednesday and GST by Tuesday, and Priya has the pricing page by Monday.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: That's it. Thanks, everyone, and please use the pricing channel for anything that changes before launch.
